findings.reason: The protected app-local comprehension declares the explicitly prohibited local variable `index`. The single inert candidate preserves the exact algorithm and app contract while using the conventional position variable `i`.

Apart from the prohibited local name, the protected solution is already the clear output-sensitive construction: scan adjacent pairs, slice only after finding `++`, and emit the corresponding one-move state. The candidate changes no control flow or asymptotic behavior.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 293 and its Python state-string-to-list contract. The Reference preserves the legal move and losing-turn semantics, both source examples in order without explanations, both constraints, and the source-permitted arbitrary output order while documenting the app's deterministic order.

The protected app-local and native sources remain structurally identical and the immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064318085. The candidate only renames the comprehension position, is inert, and has not been submitted or represented as Accepted.

The legal 16/64/256-symbol sparse-output tiers span 16x, place their sole `++` pair at the end, and distinguish checking before construction from rebuilding a complete state at every position. The candidate passes at -0.02 relative exponent and 0.98x largest ratio; a correct per-character reconstruction at every position passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +1.40 and 231.27x.

The Approach now targets the candidate's `i` variable, proves completeness from the one-to-one correspondence between legal pairs and results, gives the output-sensitive O(n + kn) derivation before the O(n^2) worst case, and covers overlaps, absent moves, and ordering.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving both examples without explanations, both constraints, the exact one-move request, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact state strings and complete output lists.
The previous suite mislabeled an invented one-move row as a sample and hid separated legal pairs; the replacement classifies additions as visible trials.
Every correctness row uses unordered_list validation because the source contract explicitly permits the generated states in any order.
Minimum length, no-move all-minus and alternating states, one legal pair at the start, middle, and end, and exact one-move output are covered.
Overlapping pairs, separated pairs, a longer plus run, and a state containing both overlap and separation verify that every adjacent ++ start is emitted exactly once without skipping neighbors.

Every expected state was independently generated by replacing each legal adjacent pair and preserving all other positions; the protected source and inert candidate matched this oracle on all 8,190 plus/minus states through length 12.
All 12 correctness cases are visible; the unchanged 16-, 64-, and 256-symbol sparse-output fixtures remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
